findings.issue: B-4 (ALB internet-facing, CloudFront prefix list optional and fail-open, no secret origin header, gateway NetworkPolicy admits the whole VPC) means a client that reaches the ALB directly can forge the entry N from the right, and so forge X-Internal-Client-Ip. This does not block slice 1. Slice 1 only computes and propagates the header, and the same bypass already applies to the existing rate-limit key, so this slice does not add exposure. The exposure grows when slice 2 makes the header the trusted source for audit, the wallet per-IP limit, login throttling and the referral IP check. The ADR currently gates only the referral check on the precondition.
findings.fix: Treat B-4 as a release gate for slice 2, not only for the referral check. Before any slice-2 consumer (wallet limit, login throttle, referral) goes to production, either make the prefix list mandatory and fail closed or verify a CloudFront secret origin header, or have the Owner explicitly accept the risk. Add a check that the slice-2 reviewers can verify: the ADR gate text or the AC-12 runbook names all four consumers.

summary: Round 2 re-review of f9a070ba..d195a937. All three of my round-1 findings are resolved. (1) Major, multi-line XFF: GatewayClientIp now uses getHeaders().getOrEmpty("X-Forwarded-For"), joins every field line with ',' in order, and counts N from the right, as RFC 9110 5.3 requires. Two tests now cover the attack. The contract test has the case 'two XFF lines, client line first' ('6.6.6.6' then '10.9.9.9, 203.0.113.7', expected 203.0.113.7). The integration test twoXffLines sends real duplicate header lines through Netty and checks that 203.0.113.11 is what the downstream receives. (2) The split(",") issue the second pass raised is fixed with split(",", -1). A trailing comma ('1.1.1.1,') now gives an empty N-th entry, which fails to parse and falls back to the socket peer. Before, the empty entry was silently dropped, which moved the chosen entry one place left onto client-controlled data. The new contract case 'trailing comma falls back' covers this. (3) Minor, bracket/zone strictness: after ']', ClientAddress now accepts only an empty remainder or ':' plus 1-5 digits. IPv4:port must also have a numeric port, and a zone id is stripped only from IPv6 text (input with a colon), so '1.1.1.1%x' is rejected. ClientAddressTest.rejects now includes '[::1]garbage', '[1.2.3.4]:x:y' and '1.1.1.1%x'. Output is still only a canonical InetAddress, and there is still no DNS lookup or added parse cost. (4) Minor, deployment precondition: the ADR now has a 'Deployment precondition' section, checked against the repo config, and the gap is filed as backlog B-4 (HIGH). That resolves the documentation ask. The rest of the delta is test-only. AC-10(c) now fails, instead of being skipped, when it cannot bind 127.0.0.2 with CI set, which is stricter. Two trivial assertions were removed from the order test, but it still pins ORDER relative to IdentityPropagationGatewayFilter. There are also import cleanups. No new endpoints, secrets, PII logging or dependencies. B-4 is an acceptable known issue for slice 1 and I do not block on it. It must be fixed or explicitly accepted by the Owner before any slice-2 consumer relies on X-Internal-Client-Ip in production, not only the referral check (the finding above).
